failure_summary.description: The tool name was copied as 'Provider — tagline…' or the provider line instead of the exact '### Provider: API' heading, so tool matching failed (T1, T5).

The Amazon marketplace `domain` was given as 'amazon.de' or 'DE' instead of the lowercase country suffix 'de' (T1, T5, T7). The search keyword also carried a generic word the tool already implies (T4).
T6 had broken brackets and parsed to zero calls. T3 listed bare parameter names with no values. T2 and T6 dropped the `optional parameters` or `required parameters` key.
'Search for these items' was answered with the same auto-complete tool for two unrelated product types. A matching search endpoint for the second retailer category was ignored (T8).
Gold optional parameters such as limit, pageSize, accept_all and timeout were not included (T2, T3, T4). No reliable rule could be derived for these.

patch.reasoning: Three systematic errors cost points in most trajectories: wrong tool-name strings, wrong value normalisation for the Amazon domain, and malformed or incomplete JSON. Each gets a short explicit rule with a template or concrete example. One further rule makes the agent pick a real search endpoint that matches the product category, instead of reusing an auto-complete tool for unrelated items.

edits.content: - `tool name` is ONLY the text after `### ` in the heading, e.g. `Amazon Pricing and Product Info: Main Endpoint` or `Wayfair: products/get-financing-offers`. Never build it from the `Provider:` line, never include the provider tagline after a dash (`Provider — long description`), and never use a bare provider name. A tool name containing ` — ` is always wrong.

edits.target: - The answer is one flat, bracket-balanced list `[{...}, {...}]` inside `<answer>` tags. Do not close the list early or leave stray brackets.
edits.content: - Write every call in exactly this shape, comma-separated, with the single closing `]` only after the last object: `[{"tool name": "A: b", "required parameters": [{"name": "x", "value": "1"}], "optional parameters": []}, {"tool name": "C: d", "required parameters": [], "optional parameters": [{"name": "q", "value": "v"}]}]`. Never write `}],` or `}]}` between calls. Never list bare parameter names (`["category", "country"]`); every entry is a `{"name", "value"}` object with a real value from the query. Never omit `required parameters` or `optional parameters`, even when empty. After writing, re-read the list and check brackets, braces and commas.

edits.target: - Do not invent parameters the query gives no basis for (random-fact ranges, max, fragment, json, notfound). Never emit a parameter with an empty value.
edits.content: - Value normalisation: for a marketplace `domain` parameter (e.g. Amazon `domain`), pass the lowercase country suffix only (`de` for 'German marketplace (amazon.de)', `com`, `co.uk`, `fr`), not the host name (`amazon.de`) and not uppercase (`DE`). Country-style values from the query ('English sports news from India') map to the matching optional params (category `sports`, country `in`, language `en`). For a search term, keep the product or entity words and descriptive adjectives. Drop only generic words that the chosen tool already implies (a movie-news search for 'Superman movies' -> `Superman`).

- 'Search for / look for / find items' means a search endpoint (`products/search`, `Search Items`, `search product`), not auto-complete, which only suggests terms. Use auto-complete only when the query asks for suggestions or when that retailer has no search endpoint in the list. When a query has several different product types (clothing vs furniture/lamps), pick the retailer or tool that fits each category separately. Do not reuse one tool for both items when another listed tool is a better fit for the second item.
